questions.question: What is the capital of Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: Jaipur is the capital of Rajasthan, also known as the Pink City.

questions.question: Which is the longest river in India?
questions.explanation: The Ganga (Ganges) is India's longest river at about 2,525 km.

questions.question: Which state has the longest coastline in India?
questions.explanation: Gujarat has the longest coastline (~1,600 km) among Indian states.

questions.question: The Kaziranga National Park is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga, famous for the one-horned rhinoceros, is in Assam.

questions.question: Which mountain range separates India from China?
questions.explanation: The Himalayas form the natural border between India and China (Tibet).

questions.question: Which is the largest state in India by area?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan is India's largest state by area (342,239 sq km).

questions.question: The river Brahmaputra is known as Tsangpo in:
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra originates in Tibet (China) as the Yarlung Tsangpo, enters India through Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.question: How many Union Territories does India currently have?
questions.explanation: India has 8 Union Territories: Delhi, Chandigarh, Puducherry, Andaman & Nicobar, Lakshadweep, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu, J&K, Ladakh.

questions.question: Jim Corbett National Park is located in:
questions.explanation: Jim Corbett National Park, India's first national park (1936), is in Uttarakhand.

questions.question: The Godavari river originates in:
questions.explanation: Godavari (the 'Dakshin Ganga') originates at Trimbakeshwar, Nashik, Maharashtra.

questions.question: Which is the smallest state in India by area?
questions.explanation: Goa is the smallest Indian state by area (3,702 sq km).

questions.question: The Western Ghats are also known as:
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats are locally called Sahyadri. The Nilgiris are part of the Western Ghats in Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: Which Indian river flows into the Arabian Sea?
questions.explanation: Narmada and Tapti flow westward into the Arabian Sea. Most other major rivers flow east into the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question: The Sundarbans mangrove forest is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in:
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans is the world's largest mangrove delta, shared between West Bengal (India) and Bangladesh.

questions.question: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which state?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram. Tamil Nadu is south of the Tropic.

questions.question: Which is the largest continent by area?
questions.explanation: Asia is the largest continent, covering about 30% of the world's land area.

questions.question: The Amazon river flows through which country?
questions.explanation: The Amazon, the world's largest river by water flow, flows primarily through Brazil before emptying into the Atlantic Ocean.

questions.question: Which is the longest river in the world?
questions.explanation: The Nile (approx 6,650 km) is generally considered the world's longest river, flowing through northeastern Africa.

questions.question: The capital of Australia is:
questions.explanation: Canberra is Australia's capital city, chosen as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.question: Which is the largest ocean?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, covering about 46% of the world's water surface.

questions.question: Mount Everest is located in:
questions.explanation: Mount Everest (8,849 m) straddles the Nepal-Tibet (China) border. The summit is on the border, with the south face in Nepal and north face in China.

questions.question: The Sahara Desert is located in:
questions.explanation: The Sahara Desert, the world's largest hot desert, spans North Africa across Algeria, Libya, Egypt, and other countries.

questions.question: Which country has the largest population in the world (2024)?
questions.explanation: India surpassed China in 2023 to become the world's most populous country with over 1.4 billion people.

questions.question: The Andes mountain range runs along which continent?
questions.explanation: The Andes are the longest mountain range in the world, running along the western coast of South America through Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, and Chile.

questions.question: The capital of Japan is:
questions.explanation: Tokyo is Japan's capital and largest city, one of the world's most populous metropolitan areas.

questions.question: The Alps mountain range is located in:
questions.explanation: The Alps span Switzerland, France, Italy, Germany, Austria, Liechtenstein, Slovenia, and Monaco.

questions.question: Which is the largest country in the world by area?
questions.explanation: Russia is the world's largest country at about 17.1 million sq km — nearly double the size of the second-largest, Canada.

questions.question: The Congo river flows through:
questions.explanation: The Congo river is the deepest river in the world and flows through the Democratic Republic of Congo in Central Africa.

questions.question: The Strait of Malacca connects:
options: Andaman Sea and South China Sea
questions.explanation: The Strait of Malacca between Malaysia and Indonesia connects the Andaman Sea (Indian Ocean) and the South China Sea (Pacific Ocean). It is one of the world's most important shipping lanes.

questions.question: Which country is known as the 'Land of the Rising Sun'?
questions.explanation: Japan is called 'Land of the Rising Sun'. The name 'Japan' in Japanese (Nihon/Nippon) means 'origin of the sun'.

questions.question: India gained independence on:
questions.explanation: India became independent on 15 August 1947. 26 January 1950 is when India became a Republic (Constitution came into effect).

questions.question: Who led the Dandi March (Salt March) of 1930?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi led the 241-mile Dandi March from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi, Gujarat, to protest the British salt tax in March-April 1930.

questions.question: Who was the first President of independent India?
questions.explanation: Dr Rajendra Prasad was the first President of India (1950–1962). Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister.

questions.question: The Battle of Plassey (1757) was won by:
questions.explanation: Robert Clive led the British East India Company to victory at Plassey in 1757 against Siraj ud-Daulah (Nawab of Bengal), beginning British supremacy in India.

questions.question: Who wrote the Indian national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana'?
questions.explanation: Jana Gana Mana was written by Rabindranath Tagore in Bengali. It was adopted as the national anthem on 24 January 1950.

questions.question: Bhagat Singh was hanged on:
questions.explanation: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru were hanged at Lahore Central Jail on 23 March 1931 for the killing of British officer Saunders.

questions.question: The Partition of India in 1947 resulted in the creation of:
questions.explanation: India was partitioned in 1947 into India (Hindu-majority) and Pakistan (Muslim-majority, comprising present-day Pakistan and Bangladesh).

questions.question: The Indian Constitution was drafted under the chairmanship of:
questions.explanation: Dr B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly and is called the chief architect of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: The Sepoy Mutiny (First War of Independence) occurred in:
questions.explanation: The Sepoy Mutiny of 1857 began in Meerut and spread across India. It is also called India's First War of Independence.

questions.question: Who gave the slogan 'Jai Hind'?
questions.explanation: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose popularised 'Jai Hind' (Long live India). He formed the Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army) during World War II.

questions.question: The Quit India Movement was launched in:
questions.explanation: The Quit India Movement (August Kranti) was launched by Gandhi on 8 August 1942 with the call 'Do or Die' (Karenge ya marenge).

questions.question: The ancient city of Harappa was located in present-day:
questions.explanation: Harappa is located in present-day Pakistan's Punjab province, in the Sahiwal district. The Harappan Civilisation existed c.2500–1750 BCE.

questions.question: Who was the first woman Prime Minister of India?
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi was India's first woman Prime Minister (1966–1977, 1980–1984).

questions.question: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on 13 April 1919 in:
questions.explanation: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred in Amritsar (Punjab), when General Dyer ordered troops to fire on a peaceful gathering.

questions.question: The Maurya Empire was founded by:
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire around 321 BCE with the help of his advisor Chanakya (Kautilya). Ashoka was his grandson.

questions.question: Who invented the telephone?
questions.explanation: Alexander Graham Bell is credited with inventing the telephone (patented 1876), though Elisha Gray also developed a similar device simultaneously.

questions.question: Penicillin, the first antibiotic, was discovered by:
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 when he observed that mould (Penicillium notatum) killed bacteria in a petri dish.

questions.question: India's first satellite was:
questions.explanation: Aryabhata, named after the Indian mathematician-astronomer, was India's first satellite, launched on 19 April 1975 by the Soviet Union.

questions.question: Chandrayaan-1 was India's first mission to:
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-1 (launched 2008) was India's first lunar mission. It discovered water molecules on the Moon's surface.

questions.question: C.V. Raman received the Nobel Prize for the discovery of:
questions.explanation: C.V. Raman won the Nobel Prize in Physics (1930) for the Raman Effect — the inelastic scattering of photons by matter.

questions.question: Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission) was launched in:
questions.explanation: Mangalyaan (MOM) was launched on 5 November 2013 and successfully entered Mars orbit on 24 September 2014. India became the first country to succeed in its first attempt.

questions.question: The internet was originally developed as:
questions.explanation: The internet originated from ARPANET (Advanced Research Projects Agency Network), a US Department of Defense project started in 1969 for resilient military communications.

questions.question: APJ Abdul Kalam is associated with India's:
questions.explanation: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam, the 'Missile Man of India', led the development of India's ballistic missile and space programmes (Agni, Prithvi, SLV-3). He later served as India's 11th President.

questions.question: The human body contains how many bones in an adult?
questions.explanation: An adult human skeleton has 206 bones. A newborn has about 270-300, which fuse as the child grows.

questions.question: The symbol of the element Gold is:
questions.explanation: Gold's symbol Au comes from the Latin 'Aurum'. Silver's symbol Ag comes from 'Argentum'.

questions.question: The first human to walk on the Moon was:
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong became the first human to walk on the Moon on 21 July 1969 during the Apollo 11 mission.

questions.question: DNA was first described by:
questions.explanation: James Watson and Francis Crick described the double helix structure of DNA in 1953, based on X-ray crystallography data from Rosalind Franklin.

questions.question: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately:
questions.explanation: The speed of light c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s (approximately 300,000 km/s). This is the universal speed limit.

questions.question: The periodic table was developed by:
questions.explanation: Dmitri Mendeleev (1869) published the first widely recognised periodic table, arranging elements by atomic mass and predicting properties of undiscovered elements.

questions.question: ISRO stands for:
questions.explanation: ISRO — Indian Space Research Organisation — was established in 1969. It is headquartered in Bengaluru.

questions.question: The Indian Constitution came into force on:
questions.explanation: The Indian Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 but came into force on 26 January 1950, which is why that date is celebrated as Republic Day.

questions.question: Article 21 of the Indian Constitution guarantees:
options: Protection of Life and Personal Liberty
questions.explanation: Article 21: 'No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.' It has been expanded to include the right to a dignified life.

questions.question: The Preamble to the Indian Constitution begins with:
questions.explanation: 'We, the People of India, having solemnly resolved to constitute India into a Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic...'

questions.question: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976) added which words to the Preamble?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist' and 'Secular' to the Preamble, making India's official description: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic.

questions.question: Lok Sabha members are elected for a term of:
questions.explanation: Members of the Lok Sabha (lower house of Parliament) are elected for a 5-year term. Rajya Sabha members serve 6-year terms.

questions.question: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is:
questions.explanation: The maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 552: 530 from states, 20 from Union Territories, and 2 nominated Anglo-Indians (the Anglo-Indian reservation was removed by the 104th Amendment in 2020).

questions.question: Under which article is the Right to Education (6-14 years) guaranteed?
questions.explanation: Article 21A (added by the 86th Amendment, 2002): Right to Free and Compulsory Education for all children aged 6-14 years.

questions.question: The Supreme Court of India was established in:
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court of India was established on 28 January 1950, replacing the Federal Court of India.

questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy are borrowed from the constitution of:
questions.explanation: The Directive Principles of State Policy were borrowed from the Irish Constitution (1937). They are guidelines for the state to establish social and economic democracy.

questions.question: Article 370 (now abrogated) gave special status to:
questions.explanation: Article 370 gave special autonomous status to Jammu & Kashmir. It was abrogated on 5 August 2019, and J&K was bifurcated into two Union Territories.

questions.question: The minimum age to vote in Indian elections is:
questions.explanation: The minimum voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment (1988).

questions.question: India's federal structure is described as:
options: Quasi-federal — strong centre with federal features
questions.explanation: India is often described as a 'quasi-federal' state — it has a strong central government (like a unitary state) with federal features (division of powers between centre and states).

questions.question: The Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) allows citizens to:
options: Approach the Supreme Court to enforce Fundamental Rights
questions.explanation: Article 32 is the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution (Ambedkar). It allows any citizen to petition the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights through writs.

questions.question: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) relates to:
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment (1992) provided constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions, establishing a three-tier system of local governance in rural India.

questions.question: The President of India is elected by:
options: Elected members of Parliament and state legislative assemblies
questions.explanation: The President is elected by an Electoral College comprising elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of state legislative assemblies.

questions.question: Who won India's first individual Olympic gold medal?
questions.explanation: Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual Olympic gold medal in 10m air rifle shooting at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.

questions.question: India won the Cricket World Cup in:
questions.explanation: India won the ICC Cricket World Cup in 1983 (50-over) under Kapil Dev, and in 2011 (50-over) under MS Dhoni.

questions.question: The highest sporting honour in India is:
questions.explanation: The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian honour, also awarded to sportspersons. Sachin Tendulkar was the first sportsperson to receive it (2014). The Khel Ratna (Major Dhyan Chand Award) is the highest sports-specific award.

questions.question: PV Sindhu won a silver medal in badminton at which Olympics?
questions.explanation: PV Sindhu won a silver medal in women's singles badminton at the 2016 Rio Olympics, becoming the first Indian woman to win an Olympic silver.

questions.question: Neeraj Chopra won India's gold medal in which event at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics?
questions.explanation: Neeraj Chopra won a gold medal in men's javelin throw at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics (held in 2021), throwing 87.58 metres.

questions.question: Major Dhyan Chand is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: Major Dhyan Chand (1905-1979) was India's legendary field hockey player, known as 'The Wizard'. India's highest sports award is named the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award.

questions.question: The Dronacharya Award is given to:
questions.explanation: The Dronacharya Award is India's highest honour for sports coaches, named after the legendary teacher Dronacharya from Mahabharata.

questions.question: India has won the most Olympic medals in which sport (all-time)?
questions.explanation: India has won 12 Olympic medals in field hockey (8 gold, 1 silver, 3 bronze) — the most in any single sport for India.

questions.question: Sania Mirza is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: Sania Mirza is India's celebrated tennis player. She has won six Grand Slam titles (all in doubles), making her one of the most successful Indian women in sports.

questions.question: The Bharat Ratna was first awarded in:
questions.explanation: Bharat Ratna was first awarded in 1954 to three recipients: C. Rajagopalachari, S. Radhakrishnan, and C.V. Raman.

questions.question: Mary Kom is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: MC Mary Kom (Manipur) is a legendary Indian boxer. She has won 8 World Amateur Boxing Championships and an Olympic bronze (2012 London).

questions.question: The first Indian woman to win a Wimbledon title was:
questions.explanation: Sania Mirza won the Wimbledon mixed doubles title in 2015 (partnering Bruno Soares). In singles, no Indian woman has won Wimbledon.

questions.question: India's 'Flying Sikh' Milkha Singh was known for:
questions.explanation: Milkha Singh (1929-2021), the 'Flying Sikh', was a legendary sprinter who narrowly missed the Olympic bronze in 400m at the 1960 Rome Olympics.

questions.question: How many gold medals did India win at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics?
questions.explanation: India won 1 gold medal at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics — Neeraj Chopra's javelin throw gold. India's total tally was 7 medals (1 gold, 2 silver, 4 bronze).

questions.question: The Arjuna Award is given to recognize:
questions.explanation: The Arjuna Award recognises outstanding achievement by sportspersons in national competitions. Named after Arjuna, the supreme archer of the Mahabharata.
